pages.title: MC3DPrint Terminal
pages.text: An $(l)Applied Energistics 2$() cable part that lists what your printers and formed Fabricators (T5-T8) can make and orders it, paid in $(l)Filament Units$() instead of ingredients.$(br2)It $(l)dispatches$(), it does not craft: ordering queues a job on a real machine, which does the work at its normal speed, RF draw and filament cost. An order costs exactly what printing it by hand would.$(br2)Needs AE2 installed. Without it, the terminal does not exist.

pages.title: The Catalog
pages.text: Every priced item appears, sorted by tier then cost.$(br2)Things you $(l)cannot$() order stay listed and greyed, with the reason: needs a higher tier, wind-only, restricted trophy, or not enough filament.$(br2)Nothing is hidden, so a greyed row tells you what to go build, and the grid does not reshuffle under your cursor as filament moves.$(br2)Search matches the item name $(l)and$() its registry id.

pages.title: The Tier Rail
pages.text: One row per tier down the left, showing the filament that could pay a cost at that tier. Hover for exact numbers.$(br2)Each row counts its own tier $(l)and every tier above it$(), because spending is down-only: a Tier 3 spool pays a Tier 1 cost, a Tier 1 spool never pays a Tier 3 one.$(br2)A single combined total would be the number that lies to you.

pages.title: Orders
pages.text: Click to order one, Shift-click for a stack.$(br2)Click one of your own orders in the list to $(l)cancel$() it. Other players' orders are theirs to cancel.$(br2)An order binds to $(l)one$() machine, and a machine runs one order at a time, so two orders never spend the same spools.$(br2)Interruptions $(l)hold$() rather than fail: no filament, no power, or nowhere to put the output all pause and resume.$(br2)If a machine loses its channel or leaves the network, the order is $(l)released$() and looks for another machine. While held with nowhere to deliver, it spends $(l)nothing$().$(br2)Filament is spent if and only if an item is delivered.

pages.title: Taking a Machine Back
pages.text: Load a disc, or drop an item in a printer's template slot, and that machine is yours again at once.$(br2)Any terminal order it was running is handed back to the queue and finds somewhere else to run. A terminal order $(l)never$() interrupts work you started by hand.
An AE2 $(item)Crafting Terminal$() ringed by eight $(item)Extrudium Crystals$().
